Subject: Re: Unexpected merchant fee on payment for BP-0422

Hi Claire — thanks for flagging this and for the remittance file.

Short answer: Redwood invoices customers for the gross subscription amount. External payment processors sometimes capture their own merchant fee before depositing the net. When that happens the customer payment appears short against the AR balance. We usually either (A) post an internal merchant-fee expense and reduce AR to match the net deposit, or (B) leave the AR balance and request the customer to remit the gross amount — practice varies depending on contract terms and VAT treatment.

Looping in Laura (finance) and Grace (payments ops) to confirm the preferred accounting fix for BluePeak and whether VAT needs an adjustment.

I attached BP-0422 for reference.

Attachment: BP-0422-invoice.pdf

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: BluePeak — merchant fee impact & proposed JE (analysis)

Ben / Grace,

I pulled the remittance and mapped it to the BP-0422 invoice. Summary: invoice gross = $48,000. Processed deposit = $46,608 (net after 2.9% processor fee = $1,392). VAT was billed on the gross invoice (VAT recorded = $3,600). The processor fee does not include VAT and was deducted from the cash settlement.

Impact: if we leave AR at gross ($48k), the bank deposit will not match and AR will remain partially open. If we book a merchant-fee accrual we can clear AR and recognize the net cash; however VAT liability was recorded on gross revenue so VAT balances will need an offset entry.

Proposed two-step journal (to reverse the unapplied AR and reflect expense):
- JE1 (accrue merchant fee): Debit Merchant Fee Expense (6400) $1,392 ; Credit Merchant Fee Accrued (2410) $1,392
- JE2 (apply net payment and clear AR): Debit Bank — Processor Settlement (1002) $46,608 ; Debit Merchant Fee Accrued (2410) $1,392 ; Credit Accounts Receivable — BluePeak (1100) $48,000

VAT adjustment (if VAT must be reduced from liability because VAT was recorded on gross but the actual cash was net): we propose a contra VAT entry at period close after confirming with tax — example: Debit VAT Payable (2100) $0* ; Credit VAT Adjustment Clearing (2420) $0* (placeholder until tax confirms).

Please note the VAT treatment depends on whether the fee is treated as a deduction from gross consideration under local tax rules. I will coordinate with Vivek for final guidance on VAT entry. Attachment: invoice_recon.xlsx (line-by-line).

If Finance and Payments Ops agree, I recommend posting JE1 immediately and JE2 once the bank deposit is confirmed and matched.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Finance Manager — Revenue Ledger
Redwood Inference

Agree with Laura's approach. Operations notes and implementation steps: 
- We will create a processor settlement clearing code to capture net deposits by processor batch (helps avoid mismatches when multiple invoices/payments are in a single remittance).
- I will upload the remittance to the settlement queue and tag the BP-0422 deposit to the batch id (SETT-2027-04-25).
- We'll post JE1 (merchant fee accrual) today for the amount in the statement so AR can be reduced during cash application.
- JE2 (final application) to be posted after bank feed reconciliation (expected by Friday 04/30).

On VAT: tagging Vivek since tax treatment will change posting — if VAT stays on gross revenue we may need an additional VAT reclaim/credit; if tax rules allow netting, we'll reduce VAT payable accordingly. Vivek — can you advise on the preferred VAT flow for US domestic SaaS when processor fee is withheld?

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Payments Operations Lead
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BluePeak — merchant fee impact & proposed JE (analysis)

Thanks for the clear write-up. For US domestic SaaS: VAT/GST is not applicable; however, for customers in VAT jurisdictions this matters. Since BluePeak is US-based and we billed VAT accidentally in a previous template (looks like an AR metadata issue), we should:

1) Reverse the VAT entry that was posted on the gross invoice (if any) and book a VAT adjustment to remove the liability.
2) Post the merchant fee accrual and clear AR per Laura's JE1/JE2 sequence.
3) Update AR invoice metadata to prevent re-billing VAT for US customers (ticket created: FIN-AR-2027-159).

I approve posting JE1 today and JE2 after bank reconciliation. Grace — proceed with settlement tagging and book JE1. Laura — coordinate VAT reversal entry as part of May close; provide exact amounts once JE1 posts.

Vivek Kulkarni
